skill.name: swarm-advanced
skill.description: Advanced orchestration patterns for coordinating Claude Flow swarms across research, development, testing, and analysis workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate multi-agent Claude Flow swarms for complex research, development, testing, and analysis projects.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown code fence false positives, not Ruby backtick execution. Four Bash examples are confirmed medium risk because they run npm or npx. No prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: External npm and npx execution guidance
remediation.suggestion: Pin Claude Flow to a reviewed stable version. Tell users to verify the package source before running commands.

remediation.issue: CLI fallback commands can affect the local environment
remediation.suggestion: Mark CLI fallbacks as manual steps that require explicit user approval and a trusted project context.

content.value_statement: Complex AI projects need clear coordination across research, coding, testing, and reporting. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable swarm patterns with MCP and CLI examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, star, and ring swarm topologies.
Provides research, development, testing, and analysis swarm patterns.
Shows MCP tool calls for initialization, agent spawning, task orchestration, memory, and monitoring.
Includes CLI fallback examples for Claude Flow swarm commands.
Covers error handling, state management, neural learning, automation, and performance monitoring.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow and related MCP tools for full execution.
Examples need adaptation to project constraints and available tools.
CLI commands should be reviewed before use in any environment.
Does not verify the security of external npm packages or target applications.

use_cases.title: Plan A Research Swarm
use_cases.description: Coordinate parallel researchers, analysts, and writers to gather sources and produce a structured report.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Full Stack Delivery
use_cases.description: Assign architecture, backend, frontend, database, testing, review, and documentation roles in one workflow.

use_cases.title: Run Distributed Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Organize unit, integration, end-to-end, performance, and security testing across specialized agents.

prompt_templates.title: Choose A Topology
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-advanced to choose a topology for my project. Explain the agent roles, task order, and monitoring approach.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Research Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-advanced to design a research swarm for this topic: [topic]. Include gathering, validation, synthesis, and reporting phases.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Development Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-advanced to create a development swarm for [application]. Define specialist agents, dependencies, checkpoints, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize A Running Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-advanced to diagnose this swarm workflow: [workflow details]. Recommend topology changes, fault handling, memory use, and metrics.

output_examples.input: Plan a research swarm for market analysis.
output_examples.output: A mesh topology with web researchers, analysts, source validators, and a report writer. The plan separates gathering, validation, synthesis, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Coordinate a full stack feature build.
output_examples.output: A hierarchical workflow with an architect as coordinator, parallel implementation roles, testing phases, review gates, and deployment readiness checks.
A star topology focused on test coordination, parallel suites, bottleneck analysis, monitoring cadence, and clear fallback steps.

best_practices: Choose the topology that matches dependency structure and coordination needs.
Assign specialized agents with clear responsibilities before running parallel work.
Monitor resource use, task status, and memory namespaces during long workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not spawn many agents before defining dependencies and ownership.
Do not run CLI fallback commands without reviewing package source and permissions.
Do not use parallel execution for tasks that require strict sequencing.

faq.question: What tools does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects Claude Flow MCP tools for full workflows and offers CLI fallback examples.

faq.question: Can I use it without Claude Flow installed?
faq.answer: You can use the planning guidance, but MCP examples and CLI workflows require Claude Flow setup.

faq.question: Which swarm topology should I start with?
faq.answer: Use mesh for research, hierarchical for development, star for testing, and ring for pipeline-style processing.

faq.question: Does it execute tasks automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides patterns and examples. Actual execution depends on available tools and user approval.

faq.question: Is this suitable for security audits?
faq.answer: It includes a security audit pattern, but users must verify tools, scope, and permission boundaries.

faq.question: How should teams adapt the examples?
faq.answer: Replace sample tasks, agents, namespaces, and monitoring settings with project-specific requirements.
